  PROBLEM: When the expected base branch cannot be resolved, `_security_fix_contained` propagates the lookup error and the checker exits with code 2, causing repeated retries without surfacing the underlying failure.

  PROBLEM: A commit pushed between reading the audit log and reading the branch HEAD can make the checker reject a successful audit result as “moved.”
  WHY: The audit log records the earlier SHA while the subsequent HEAD read sees the new SHA; Qwen and GLM state that a moved branch intentionally requires re-audit.

  WHY: Unlike the `Target branch:` capture, this capture permits only whitespace after the branch name; GLM characterizes the asymmetry as fail-closed and says it does not affect current generated metadata.

  PROBLEM: When `--security-fix-base` is set and the expected base branch no longer exists, `gh_api` raises `ReadError`, which propagates through `check_issues` to `main()` and returns exit 2.
  WHY: The checker treats exit 2 as a transient read failure and retries hourly without surfacing that the deleted branch is blocking the security cycle.
- .github/workflows/validate.yml:215-218 (jq Integration branch capture) | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The `Integration branch:` capture permits only whitespace to end of line after the branch name, so a backtick-quoted branch followed by trailing prose fails capture.
  WHY: An `Integration branch:` line such as `` `orchestrator/project-4139` (integration branch) `` would be rejected as `malformed issue base`; current generated metadata does not include trailing prose, so the risk is theoretical in the current pipeline.

  PROBLEM: A commit pushed after the audit log is read but before the branch HEAD is read can cause the checker to reject a valid, successful audit result as “moved.”

  WHY: The checker then silently retries without surfacing the underlying repository access failure.
